relationships.description: The operation declares the path, query, header or cookie inputs a caller supplies with this method-path pair, each of which may also be shared as a reusable component parameter.
relationships.evidence: The operation's 'parameters' array in the OpenAPI document lists the parameter inline or via a $ref to components/parameters, or the handler signature binds it with a @PathVariable/@RequestParam/@Header annotation.

relationships.description: The operation accepts the described request payload as the body a client sends when invoking this body-bearing method, possibly reusing a shared component request body.
relationships.evidence: The operation's 'requestBody' field defines the payload inline or by $ref to components/requestBodies, or the controller action binds a @RequestBody/body DTO argument.

relationships.description: The operation overrides the base URLs at which it can be called, so requests to this method-path pair are sent to the listed server locations rather than the document defaults.
relationships.evidence: An operation-level 'servers' array in the OpenAPI document lists the server URL for this method-path pair.

relationships.description: The operation is grouped under the named tag category so documentation and tooling present it alongside other operations in the same group.
relationships.evidence: The operation's 'tags' array contains the tag name that is declared in the root 'tags' list, or the controller carries an @Tag/@Api annotation with that name.

relationships.description: The operation is one of the endpoints contained in the document's Paths map, existing only as an entry under its path item within that container.
relationships.evidence: The OpenAPI document's 'paths' object has a path-template key whose PathItem contains this HTTP method entry.

relationships.description: The operation owns its status-code map of possible outcomes, which has no meaning outside this single method-path pair.
relationships.evidence: The operation object in the OpenAPI document contains a 'responses' field keyed by status codes or 'default'.

relationships.description: The operation embeds an inline data-shape definition, in a parameter, request body or response, that exists only as part of this operation's contract.
relationships.evidence: An inline 'schema' object (not a $ref) appears nested within this operation's parameters, requestBody content or responses content in the OpenAPI document.

relationships.description: The operation returns the described HTTP outcome to the caller for the given status code when the corresponding result occurs.
relationships.evidence: The operation's 'responses' map has a status-code entry pointing to this Response, and the handler code returns that status with the matching body.

relationships.description: The operation makes a user-perceivable product feature programmatically invocable, acting as the API entry point through which clients trigger that feature.
relationships.evidence: The feature specification or product backlog item lists the endpoint as its API, or the frontend code for the feature calls this method and path.

relationships.description: The operation is the concrete callable contract through which an internal application function's behavior is carried out when the endpoint is hit.
relationships.evidence: The route handler for this method and path delegates to the module or service class that implements the application function.

relationships.description: The operation automates one or more activities of a business process so that invoking it performs that business step in software.
relationships.evidence: Process documentation or a BPMN service task names this endpoint as the implementation of a process activity, or the handler executes the process's workflow step.

relationships.description: The operation contributes concretely toward a stakeholder goal by providing behavior that moves the organization in the intended direction.
relationships.evidence: A traceability matrix, ADR or epic links the endpoint to the goal it was built to advance.

relationships.description: The operation provides the capability whose use produces a measurable end result the organization targets.
relationships.evidence: An outcome definition or OKR document cites this endpoint as the delivery mechanism, and metrics for the outcome are computed from its usage.

relationships.description: The operation points to the application service it is one of the access points for, identifying which offered behavior this endpoint belongs to.
relationships.evidence: An x-extension or description on the operation names the application service, or the service catalog entry lists this method and path among its operations.

relationships.description: The operation identifies the business channel, such as a customer portal or partner gateway, through which its functionality is offered to business actors.
relationships.evidence: Channel documentation or an operation extension field names the business interface (e.g. 'Partner Portal') that surfaces this endpoint.

relationships.description: The operation points to the business service whose value it helps deliver, tying the technical endpoint to the externally offered business offering.
relationships.evidence: The service catalogue or an operation-level extension/tag maps this endpoint to the named business service.

relationships.description: The operation links to documentation hosted outside the API description that explains its usage in more detail.
relationships.evidence: The operation object contains an 'externalDocs' field with the documentation URL.

relationships.description: The operation points to another operation, for example as a follow-on call via a response link or a related endpoint, without depending on it to execute.
relationships.evidence: A response 'links' entry in this operation names the other operation by operationId or operationRef, or its description cross-references it.

relationships.description: The operation uses a reusable named schema to define the shape of one of its inputs or outputs without owning that schema.
relationships.evidence: A '$ref: #/components/schemas/...' appears within this operation's parameters, requestBody or responses content.

relationships.description: The operation identifies the protected resource that authorization decisions are made about when this endpoint is invoked.
relationships.evidence: The access-control model or authorization middleware configuration maps this method and path to the named secure resource.

relationships.description: The operation names a tag defined at document level to categorize itself, relying on the tag's descriptive metadata for documentation grouping.
relationships.evidence: The operation's 'tags' array includes a name matching an entry in the root 'tags' array.

relationships.description: The operation is recorded as an attack surface against which a modelled threat, such as injection or credential stuffing, applies.
relationships.evidence: The threat model entry lists this endpoint's method and path as an affected entry point.

relationships.description: The operation is instrumented under the named tracing configuration, which determines how spans for its requests are sampled, propagated and exported.
relationships.evidence: The service hosting the handler initializes the TracerProvider with this configuration, or a per-route sampling rule names this endpoint.

relationships.description: The operation can only be invoked by a caller holding the specified permission, which is checked at the endpoint before the handler executes.
relationships.evidence: The handler is annotated with @PreAuthorize/@RequiresPermission naming the permission, or the operation's security requirement lists the corresponding OAuth scope.

relationships.description: The operation's access decisions are produced by evaluating the named security policy whenever a request arrives at this endpoint.
relationships.evidence: The API gateway or policy engine configuration (e.g. OPA, XACML, Envoy RBAC) binds the policy to this method and path.

relationships.description: The operation's design complies with a stated restriction such as a mandated protocol, data jurisdiction or contractual term.
relationships.evidence: An ADR or compliance review records that this endpoint conforms to the constraint, e.g. it uses the mandated auth standard or regional host.

relationships.description: The operation implements the protective behavior a countermeasure calls for, such as input validation, rate limiting or re-authentication on this endpoint.
relationships.evidence: The countermeasure's implementation record points to this endpoint, and the handler or gateway route applies the corresponding validation or rate-limit configuration.

relationships.description: The operation provides the verifiable behavior demanded by a requirement, so the requirement's acceptance criteria are met by calling this endpoint.
relationships.evidence: The requirement's acceptance tests exercise this method and path, or the traceability matrix links the requirement ID to the operationId.

relationships.description: The operation provides functionality used by people acting in a business role, such as an approver or claims adjuster, to carry out their responsibilities.
relationships.evidence: The role's access mapping grants it this endpoint, or user-story documentation for the role names the endpoint as the one they call.

relationships.description: Successful invocation of the operation causes the application to emit a named state-change event that other behavior reacts to.
relationships.evidence: The handler publishes the event (e.g. 'OrderCreated') to a message broker or event bus after processing the request.

relationships.description: A call to the operation initiates an instance of a business process, such as submitting a claim starting the claims-handling workflow.
relationships.evidence: The handler starts a workflow instance in the process engine (e.g. Camunda startProcessInstanceByKey) or the BPMN start event references this endpoint.

relationships.description: Invoking the operation causes the API to later issue the described outbound request to the consumer-supplied URL.
relationships.evidence: The operation's 'callbacks' field defines the callback with a runtime expression such as {$request.body#/callbackUrl}, and the handler schedules the outbound HTTP call.

relationships.description: The operation is served through an application interface, such as a mounted controller or gateway endpoint, which is the channel through which requests reach it.
relationships.evidence: The route is registered on the controller or router mounted as that interface, e.g. the method is declared in the @RestController class bound to that base path.

relationships.description: The operation expects callers to present credentials using the named mechanism, such as a bearer token or API key, before it is executed.
relationships.evidence: The operation's 'security' array references the scheme name registered under components.securitySchemes.

relationships.description: The operation depends on an infrastructure capability, such as a database, cache, queue or identity provider, to process its requests.
relationships.evidence: The handler's code path calls a client for the infrastructure service (e.g. a Redis or S3 SDK call), or deployment config wires that service's connection into the endpoint's service.

notes: composes api.paths is inverted: Paths contains PathItems containing operations. composes/references api.schema and aggregates/references api.tag overlap (inline vs $ref only). delivers api.response duplicates composes api.responses. realizes goal/outcome should be supports/delivers. realizes and triggers businessprocess overlap.
